title: Continuous Phase Foliations Create Analytic Caustic Collars

issues.location: sec:joint, proof of Lemma joint:compatibility (cyclic inverse)
issues.description: The formula ∂^{-1}=t0 R_q T_{t0/2} on ker Π is only a right inverse. R_q does not map ker Π into itself, so the actual inverse is (1−Π)R_q composed with the half-shift. This does not affect the norm bound C q|t0|.
issues.evidence: (T−1)R_q = 1−Π, checked by direct summation using T^q = id on 2π-periodic functions. R_q f is not in general in ker Π.

coverage: Read all five sections in full. Checked by hand: the reflection and twist signs (geo:reflection, geo:twists); the opposite-sign property; the separation-barrier lemma (quarter-turn exclusion, barrier rule, sign intervals); the constant-translation recurrence argument on the simultaneous cover (finite measure via the relative bound, recurrence to a point); the rational-passage argument; graph limits; ordering and the grazing limit; plateau exclusion; stationary-chain closure and the action derivative. Checked numerically (mpmath): the normalized-action integration-by-parts identity and the generating relations p=−S1, p'=S2. Checked the universal cubic and the vanishing quartic (2a4=a3'), the endpoint terms in W_q', the Wiener operator column sums and the exponent balance, the initial error split, the Newton majorant exponents (ratio C P^{-r0} 2^{r0+1−j}), and the real-uniqueness contraction. In the joint section: E and a at t=0, the linearization ∂(a∂w)+(Ew)' (with c± and T_{±t/2}a=c±/t), the parameter-jet formula, mean zero, the Dirichlet inverse bound q²t0² ≤ CQ², the contraction exponent Q^7, the conjugacy G∘ỹ1=G+t0 and the exact solution V*, the resonant and nonresonant divisor bounds, the buffer index constraints of both divisions, and the initializer/induction exponents (C d0^{2B+3} 2^{4B+4−(2B+3)i}). In the caustics section: the invariance relation, evenness of p, the inward expansion r Θ_y² t²/8, and the support-function convex-body and collar argument. Not verified: the imported companion results NB Lemma 2.3, Proposition 2.4, Lemma 3.5 and Theorem 1.2, which are used as black boxes.
main_claim: A smooth, strictly convex planar billiard with positive curvature, whose grazing annulus is continuously foliated by individually invariant essential curves, has an analytic boundary and a jointly analytic collar of convex caustics. By the companion paper's physical-collar theorem, it is therefore an ellipse.
sibling_notes: Companion paper NB (Rigidity-of-Smooth-Billiards-with-a-Continuous-Caustic-Collar) was partially audited by a sibling branch with no_gap_found. This paper's own contributions (the graph and rational-periodicity argument, and building the caustics from the stationary family V) do not depend on the foliation coinciding with V at irrational parameters: the caustics are built directly from V, and the foliation is only used for rational compatibility. There is no circularity: NB's analytic estimates are stated for arbitrary inputs, and NB's rigidity theorem is applied only after the physical collar has been built.
